summary: Independent cold medRxiv screening audit passed with zero blockers across all clinical ethics, privacy, safety, authorship, attribution, and numerical coherence gates. The manuscript is a purely retrospective methodological and secondary observational study on two publicly available de-identified datasets (PhysioNet 2019 sepsis and Yale New Haven ED triage; 600,154 total encounters across five hospitals) plus synthetic simulations, with an explicit 45 CFR 46.102(e) IRB/informed-consent exemption statement, zero patient-identifiable details, non-prescriptive retrospective framing disclaiming bedside readiness, sole human authorship, transparent Google Antigravity/Gemini AI workflow disclosure, full COI/funding/open-data-code declarations, and verified internal mathematical and numerical consistency.

warnings.detail: Explicitly include the word 'retrospective' in the Abstract when introducing the 600,154 multi-hospital encounters so the observational, non-prospective study design is immediately clear to medRxiv triage screeners.
Replace 'deploying zero-shot onto Campus B' with 'evaluating zero-shot on Campus B' (matching main.tex:L225) to avoid any ambiguity with live prospective clinical deployment.

The stripped Track B3 column list includes the raw field label `name` alongside demographic variables; briefly clarify that this is a non-PII categorical/site schema column in the public de-identified Yale dataset rather than patient names to prevent false-positive PII queries during medRxiv screening.

The AI-Assisted Workflows Disclosure transparently credits Google Antigravity, Gemini models, and human verification; optionally specifying the exact Gemini model version(s) used would further strengthen computational reproducibility.
